To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fear of pain related reinjury, quadricep weakness, and reduced self reported function are the primary reasons for not returning to pre-injury sports participation at one year following ACL reconstruction.
fear of pain and quadriceps strength are associated with function in patients who do not return to sport because of fear of pain or lack of confidence.

patients who do not return to sports after ACL reconstruction because of fear of injury or lack of confidence have greater pain related fear, quadriceps weakness and reduced function than those who return to sports.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients who are fearful of returning to sport after ACL reconstruction have worse physical impairment, psychosocial measures, and function than those who are not fearful.
the fear of pain and the quadriceps weakness are the two most important factors to consider for return to sport.
fear of reinjury is associated with poorer physical and functional recovery after ACL reconstruction and may be a risk factor for not returning to preinjury levels of sport.
The main takeaway from our work is that

patients reporting fear of movement/re-injury as a barrier to return to sport are older, have greater fear of pain, lower quadriceps strength and function, and are less likely to return to pre-injury sport participation.

patients with fear of reinjury and/or lack of confidence who are not returning to sport have significantly worse outcomes compared with those who are returning to sport, and that fear of reinjury may influence outcomes independent of pain.
patients who do not return to sport due to fear of reinjury and/or lack of confidence have significantly worse physical and psychosocial outcomes than those who return to sport.
